curated.notes: Aristocrats go-wide: Caesar sacrifices an attacker-adjacent creature on attack for tokens, cards or damage, so the deck wants to attack every turn with a wide board and keep token makers running (Assemble the Legion, Bastion of Remembrance, Pitiless Plunderer, Skullclamp). PLAY_AGGRO and always-on token abilities are the heuristic levers; Forge's ARISTOCRATS strategy is detected from the commander text on its own. No tutors in the list, so key cards act as discard protection and Monte Carlo plan pieces.
curated.by: hand, from the decklist and Forge's plan detectors (DESIGN.md §19)

playbook.notes: Cast rules: the mana rocks first; Caesar as soon as there is another creature for his trigger; Heroic Reinforcements only before combat with three attackers to pump; Wasteland Raider only when the opponents have creatures to give up (everyone sacrifices); then the engines and anthems (Marshal's Anthem among them: Forge's AI never casts it, AI:RemoveDeck:All) and the creatures. The removal, the sweepers, the X spells and the instants stay Forge's. Trigger rule: Caesar's attack trigger is taken whenever there is a token to give up. Under the shipped go-wide attack. Shipped 2026-11-11 as version 3 after ab-run #9: on the 200 tables of run #6 (seed 20261141) it wins 51 where stock wins 34 and the attack-only version 2 wins 32 (+8.5 points against stock, 95% +1 to +16, 37 tables won only by it against 20 only by stock, exact test 0.03). The same cast rules without the trigger rule win 41, with the trigger taken every time 44, and every time under the pressure attack 45: all four candidates beat stock and this one was the best of the four, so a confirming run on tables it has not seen is queued (demo-data/ab/2026-11-11-ab-v7/hail-caesar.json, DESIGN.md §22).
